subject: physics_2
question_text: Define focal length and radius of curvature of a concave lens.

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed pp.9-10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked physically: each lens surface is a part of a sphere and R is that sphere's radius (one R per surface); for a concave lens the principal focus is virtual — parallel rays appear to diverge from F — and f is measured from the optical centre to F.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ray Optics and Optical Instruments · 2 marks

steps.label: Radius of curvature
lines: Each surface of a lens is a part of a sphere.
The radius of that sphere is called the
radius of curvature R of that surface.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the sphere — the surface is a part of it, and R is that sphere's radius.
steps.why: A lens face is ground as a part of a sphere, so the only complete definition names that sphere and takes its radius. Each of the two faces has its own R.
common_mistakes: Giving the focal length as the radius of curvature. R belongs to one surface; f belongs to the whole lens.
Forgetting that a lens has two surfaces, each with its own radius of curvature.

recall.must_convey: That the radius of curvature is the radius of the sphere of which the lens surface is a part.
accept: radius of the sphere of which the surface is a part
each surface is part of a sphere and R is that sphere's radius
the lens surface belongs to a sphere and its radius is the radius of curvature
surface oka sphere lo part, daani radius ye R
reject: distance from the optical centre to the principal focus

steps.memory_tip: R lives on one face of the lens: face → sphere → that sphere's radius.

steps.label: Focal length
lines: Rays parallel to the principal axis, after
refraction through a concave lens, appear to
come from a fixed point on the axis — the
The distance from the optical centre of the
lens to the principal focus is the focal

lines.text: f = optical centre to principal focus

steps.margin_note: Second mark. For a concave lens say appear to come from — the focus is virtual.
steps.why: A concave lens spreads the parallel rays out, so they never actually meet — only their backward extensions meet at F. The words appear to come from are what make the definition correct for a concave lens.
common_mistakes: Saying the rays pass through F. For a concave lens they only appear to come from F.
Measuring f from the surface of the lens. It is measured from the optical centre.

recall.must_convey: That the focal length is the distance from the optical centre to the principal focus, the point parallel rays appear to come from after refraction.
accept: distance between the optical centre and the principal focus

steps.memory_tip: f joins the two special points of the lens: optical centre and principal focus.

insider_note: Two definitions, one mark each — the words a part of a sphere and appear to come from carry them.
